name: rotor-hover
note: The hover half of rotorcraft-v2 without its 3 min fixed-wing prefix, so it actually gets flown, and the first card able to measure the v0.58 rotorcraft branch now that the probe order is fixed. LIVENESS IS A COLUMN NOW: read heloOk = 1 on every rotorcraft row (v1.0.0 added heloOk/fbwOk/canOk) and one '[helofbw]' line per spawn in LogOutput.log. All 48 R39 captures had heloOk false and measured the pre-v0.58 law - the rate-normalised helo command, the wMaxP/wMaxY authority bound and the tilt-driven blend were all inert, and the airframes were flown by the fixed-wing direct-P term with HeliYawScale = 2.0 bolted on, which is precisely the configuration the v0.58 comment says limit-cycles. THE YAW SEGMENTS ARE 50 s, NOT 15, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THIS EDIT. The measured rotorcraft failure is a rail-to-rail yaw relay at 0.11-0.19 Hz (R39-rotor 1c); osc_mode correctly needs four periods of evidence before it publishes a frequency, and four periods of 0.109 Hz is 36.7 s. Against 15 s segments the detector published wobbleFreqHzAzErr NULL on every cell while wobbleCoherenceAzErr sat at 0.49 across five signals at once - the instrument was behaving and the CARD was too short. 50 s leaves ~37 s of settled window after the 10-13 s slew-in, which resolves down to 0.108 Hz. Do not shorten them back. PASS: terminal |azErr| < 2 deg on all three airframes, stickRailPctY < 10%, wobbleCoherenceAzErr below 0.3 with no frequency published in 0.08-0.5 Hz. FAIL: the R39 signature returns - pedal railed > 40%, iYaw alternating between +/-iCap, |azErr| amplitude > 15 deg at 0.10-0.40 Hz. ENTRY IS A REAL HOVER: startSpeed 0 is DECLARED, not absent - since v1.0.0 the harness places the aircraft at 0 m/s at startAlt and calls ChaseController.Forget every replicate, instead of reading the 0 as 'unset' and spawning at DroneSpawnSpeed. The 48 captures in debugtests/R39-rotor.md were flown under the old reading, at 6-110 m/s in forward flight with NO per-replicate reset (no '# entry' header on any of them); they are not hover data and are not comparable with anything flown from this card. That reset is also why repeat is now 4 rather than 1 - the old 'one replicate per hand-established hover' rule was a consequence of the fallthrough, not of the card. The airframe list names the three rotorcraft outright: left empty it fell through to Drone/DroneAirframe (a fixed-wing jet) and cls then refused the card on every lane. A tiltwing/VTOL must already be in the HOVER configuration (a card never writes customAxis1). THE COLLECTIVE IS NOT OWNED BY THIS CARD AND CANNOT BE: ScenarioPlayer.OwnInputs returns early at EntrySpeed <= 0 by deliberate design (its 'declared-zero-ok' comment - a fixed throttle at zero airspeed is a climb, not a trim), so ci.throttle keeps the last value the built-in level-hold wrote, TestDrone.HoldThrottle = 0.60, for the whole card. Expect a slow CLIMB (R39 measured +81 to +321 m per capture) and read positionRMSM / driftRateMS as containing that vertical component. Not fixable from a card file: a config pin on Scenario/ScenarioThrottle is read AFTER the early return, so it would do nothing. startAlt 2500 m, for two reasons: it is a hover altitude R39 already proved flyable (rotorcraft reached 2761 m), and it survives the operator forgetting Drone/DroneAltDeckM - at the 3000 default the decks land at 1000 and 4000 m, both above the 500 m card floor, so the batch is degraded rather than lost. SET Drone/DroneAltDeckM = 0 ANYWAY: with a 3-key roster the Latin-square diagonal puts lanes 0 and 2 low and lane 1 high, i.e. one airframe at a different air density from the other two. count 6 over the 3-key list = TWO LANES PER AIRFRAME, wrapping, and it costs nothing: lanes fly concurrently, so the wall clock is set by replicates per lane. It is insurance against task #85 - R40 lost 1 lane in 10 to a placement velocity blow-up ('aircraft gone', which is a FATAL abort and takes the lane's remaining replicates with it), and with one lane per airframe that would delete a whole airframe from the answer. It also happens to balance the deck 2x2 if the operator forgets Drone/DroneAltDeckM: the Latin-square diagonal gives every airframe one low and one high lane at count 6, where it gave a fixed deck per airframe at count 3. R42 VERDICT (v1.0.1, at the SHIPPED heliFwd=60/heliHover=20 -- R41 flew a stale v0.43 150/40 and its rotor verdict is void): CARD VALID, and its PASS criterion is met by two of three airframes. QuadVTOL1 passes emphatically and reproduces R41 to 2-3 decimals (terminal 0.0000-0.0125, stickRailPctY 9.0-9.2%, no frequency published in 0.08-0.5 Hz). AttackHelo1 now passes the <2 deg bar it failed in R41 (hoveryawL terminal 7.41 -> 1.77) -- see LAW-LEDGER.md H6/X29. UtilityHelo1 still aborts 8/8 on the altitude floor (H5): it sinks at -24..-29 m/s on the fixed HoldThrottle 0.60 and the collective fix is not in the deployed DLL, so those aborts are EXPECTED, not a finding. READ THIS BEFORE RE-FLYING: the config change is a structural NO-OP on most of this card. speedRamp clamps to 1.0 for any vFwd <= 20 and for ANY negative vFwd, so QuadVTOL1 (vFwd -0.4..-5.8 throughout) and UtilityHelo1 (6-10 m/s) fly byte-comparable numbers under both configs; only AttackHelo1's hoveryawL leg is a real contrast. NOT AN A/B: this card declares no armToggle, so no arm= appears on any capture and the v1.0.1 arm=-1 warm-up fix cannot be exercised here (ledger O14).
